main_body: Flat sand ground patch (desert), a seamless terrain tile pattern with scattered lighter and darker speckles and small dune dashes
top_band: none - terrain ground tile, no standing object, no top/front split
evidence: The candidate is a flat sand ground texture repeating every 16px with speckles and small light dune dashes. It is terrain, not a standing object, so the top/front contract does not apply. No receding side faces and no elevation drawing, so there is nothing to fail on view grounds.

style.evidence: Sand ground has a base tan with about 4 tones (pale cream highlights, light tan, mid tan base, darker brown-orange specks). Texture is scattered single-pixel dots plus short 3px dune dashes, so no 5x5 flat areas. However the pattern repeats visibly every 16px with identical dashes in a grid-like arrangement, and the speckles are sparse and low contrast. This is thinner than the grass reference, which has clumps, tufts and a dark shadow variant, and the paving reference, which has stones shaded individually. Per-tile colour count is probably around 5-7, below the reference median of about 10. Uniform tiling reads as mechanical and the variation is shallow, so a careful artist would see it as somewhat flatter than the reference.
